official.application_cycle: Intake 2027/2028 (current list 'Application Deadlines for Intake 2027/2028', ST42 - EPOS Deadlines, Stand 06/2026; one course, Development Management at RU Bochum, runs a two-year intake cycle with next intake 2028)
official.status_note: The current EPOS scholarship call covers the postgraduate courses on the Intake 2027/2028 deadline list; DAAD awards scholarships subject to funds being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), and no new courses were admitted to the EPOS programme list in 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official EPOS FAQ (Stand 06/2026): 'You do not pay for the tuiton fees, but there may be registration or enrollment fees you have to pay. Please contact the university.'
benefits: Depending on academic level, monthly payments of 992 euros for graduates or 1,300 euros (1,400 euros beginning with February 2026) for doctoral candidates
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, unless these expenses are covered by the home country or another source of funding
Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may receive a monthly rent subsidy
Monthly allowance for accompanying members of family under certain circumstances
For German-taught courses, the scholarship includes a preparatory 6-month German language course in Germany
eligibility: Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from the countries on the DAAD EPOS list of eligible countries (DAC list of developing and newly industrialised countries)

The typical scholarship holder works for a public authority or a state or private company in a developing country, engaged in planning and execution of directives and projects with emphasis on development policies in technological, economic or social areas
Holds a Bachelor's degree (normally four years) in a related subject
Has completed an academic degree with far above average results (upper third) and at least two years of related professional experience after the first degree (bachelor) at the time of application
Academic degrees should normally not be more than six years old (the FAQ confirms there is no age limit but the latest degree should not be older than six years)
Applicants who have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered
requirements: Applications have only to be sent to the respective course directly; applications sent to the DAAD will not be forwarded to the course or university
You can apply for up to three courses; if applying to more than one course, list the courses in order of priority in the DAAD application forms and do not change the priorities
The complete applications have to be submitted in English or German to be considered; incomplete applications cannot be considered

One uniform letter of motivation must be submitted to all postgraduate degree programmes of your choice, explaining the choice of courses and prioritisation; if this information is ignored, the application cannot be considered or an already awarded scholarship might be withdrawn

For study courses in German (scholarship includes a preparatory 6-month German language course in Germany): successful passing of DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before the start of the study course, therefore a minimum German language level of B1 at the time of application, evidenced by a current certificate
For courses in English: proof of adequate language skills according to the regulations of the respective course
documents: EPOS application form (Word document), typed or clearly legible
Curriculum vitae in reverse chronological order without unexplained gaps, using the europass template
One letter of motivation with detailed reference to academic, professional and personal reasons (uniform across all chosen courses, explaining the priority order)
Letter of recommendation from the current employer, on official letterhead, signed and stamped, of current date and not in a sealed envelope
Certificate(s) of employment showing at least two years of relevant work experience after the Bachelor's degree, ideally including a guarantee of re-employment upon returning home
selection_criteria: Candidates fulfil the necessary academic requirements and can be expected to successfully complete a study programme in Germany (above-average result for first academic exam - top performance third, language skills)
Candidates have a Bachelor degree (usually a four-year course) in an appropriate subject
Candidates have at least two years of professional experience

Candidates can prove their motivation is development-related and be expected to take on social responsibility and initiate and support processes of change in their personal and professional environment after their training/scholarship
coverage: Monthly scholarship payment of 992 euros for graduates (Master's track)
Monthly scholarship payment of 1,300 euros for doctoral candidates, 1,400 euros beginning with February 2026
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, unless these expenses are covered by the home country or another source of funding
Monthly rent subsidy under certain circumstances
Monthly allowance for accompanying members of family under certain circumstances; tuition fees are not charged, though registration or enrollment fees may be payable to the university
application_method: Step 1: You send your complete application(s) directly to the according postgraduate course.
Step 2: A selection committee at the course suggests potential candidates for a DAAD scholarship.
Step 3: The suggested candidates will be contacted by DAAD to upload their complete application to the DAAD Portal.
Step 4: The selection process will be finalized, and the suggested candidates will be informed accordingly.
If shortlisted there will be a telephone-interview with the university staff; this interview may only be conducted by the applicant (FAQ).
official.application_route: Apply directly to the chosen postgraduate course (up to three, prioritised) - applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded; DAAD portal upload happens only after a course nominates you.
official.citizenship_residency: Graduates from the countries on the DAAD EPOS list of eligible countries (DAC list); applicants resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is exclusively for foreign graduates from development and newly industrialised countries on the DAAD EPOS eligible-countries list.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Individual scholarships exclusively for postgraduate courses in Germany listed on the current EPOS deadline list; the FAQ confirms the scholarship is only granted for the entire duration of courses listed in the most current booklet.
official.description: With its development-oriented postgraduate study programmes, the DAAD promotes the training of specialists from development and newly industrialised countries. The scholarships offer foreign graduates from all disciplines with at least two years' professional experience the chance to take a postgraduate or Master's degree at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases to take a doctoral degree.
official.program_type: Government scholarship - DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS), funded subject to provision of funds by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
official.english_requirement: For courses in English: proof of adequate language skills according to the regulations of the respective course - recent proof of English skills: IELTS or TOEFL (the institutional TOEFL is not accepted). For courses taught in German: minimum German level B1 at the time of application and successful passing of DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before the start of the study course.

applicant_utility.summary: EPOS is a nomination-based scholarship: you never apply to the DAAD itself - you apply directly to up to three listed postgraduate courses, ranked by priority, and each course's selection committee nominates candidates for the DAAD award, who then upload the full application to the DAAD portal. Master's-track holders receive EUR 992 per month plus payments towards health, accident and liability insurance and a travel allowance, tuition fees are not charged (though registration or enrolment fees may be), and the doctoral track pays EUR 1,300 (EUR 1,400 from February 2026). The two hard filters are country eligibility (the DAC list) and the bar on having been resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from DAC-listed countries with a four-year Bachelor's in the top third, at least two years of development-related work experience, and a course on the current EPOS list that matches their career track.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is on the current EPOS eligible-countries list and pick courses from the current Intake 2027/2028 deadline list (ST42, Stand 06/2026)
Collect employment certificates covering a full two years after the Bachelor's, plus a current employer letter on letterhead with signature, stamp and current date
Sit IELTS or TOEFL early (the institutional TOEFL is not accepted); for German-taught courses secure a B1 certificate before you apply
Build one Europass CV with no unexplained gaps and one uniform motivation letter that explicitly justifies each chosen course and the priority order
Keep a complete PDF set of every document ready - you upload to the DAAD portal only if a course nominates you
common_rejection_risks: Sending the application to the DAAD instead of the course - DAAD will not forward it and it cannot be considered
A motivation letter that does not explain the chosen courses and their priority ranking (an awarded scholarship might even be withdrawn)
Employment certificates that do not evidence two full years of relevant post-Bachelor experience
A latest degree older than six years, or more than 15 months' residence in Germany at the application deadline
Anything incomplete or not in English or German; missing certified translations for non-German/English certificates
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Semester, registration or enrolment fees at the university, living costs above EUR 992 per month, dependants' costs unless family allowances are granted, and any travel already covered by your home country or another funding source.
document_audit: Employer recommendation letter must be current, on official letterhead, signed and stamped, and not in a sealed envelope
Transcripts need an explanation of the grading system if it is not part of the transcript
Applicants from the People's Republic of China are asked to submit an APS certificate with the application
Each chosen course may require additional documents beyond the DAAD list - check the course website before submitting
alerts: There is no central deadline: each listed course sets its own, and the FAQ notes the majority of the selection process is finished in March - once a course deadline has passed, you cannot still apply
The call is made subject to BMZ funds being provided, so funding availability is not guaranteed by the DAAD itself
Funding applies only to courses on the current list - a Master's programme outside the booklet cannot be funded
German-taught tracks require DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before the course starts, which cannot be reached without prior German of at least B1 level
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply directly to each chosen course (up to three, prioritised, complete and in English or German) - the course committee nominates candidates - DAAD contacts nominees to upload the complete application to the DAAD portal - final selection and notification, with a telephone interview by university staff if shortlisted.

official.deadline_note: Calls are fixed two-week windows published roughly eight months before each selection meeting: the current call runs 1-14 October 2026 (selection meeting May 2027, earliest scholarship start 1 July 2027); further calls run 1-14 February 2027, 1-14 June 2027 and 1-14 October 2027. Applications must be complete and received within the window - there is no grace period.
official.application_cycle: Fixed two-week calls a year; current call 1-14 October 2026 with selection meeting in May 2027 and earliest possible start of scholarship 1 July 2027 (subsequent calls: 1-14 February 2027, 1-14 June 2027, 1-14 October 2027)
official.status_note: The current call is open from 1 to 14 October 2026; all complete applications received during a call are included in the selection procedure and there is no limit on the number of applications accepted.
benefits: Ph.D. candidates receive a monthly stipend of EUR 1,750
A research allowance of up to EUR 100 may be paid at the end of each year to support academic work (the FAQ describes a monthly research cost allowance of EUR 100 for journeys made within Germany)
Contribution towards health insurance costs of 50% of documented costs, to a maximum of EUR 170 a month, for scholars whose health insurance is not covered by employment
Family and childcare allowances, and further funding for childcare through a reallocation of scholarship funds from the final year of funding ('time for money')
Grants for travel and additional living expenses for research purposes, laboratory visits or conferences abroad
Academic support: summer academies, research groups, language courses, workshops and supervision by liaison professors
eligibility: The doctoral candidate has been accepted for a doctoral programme at a German university where the thesis will also be submitted; nationality is irrelevant (the FAQ confirms non-German citizens doing a doctorate at a German university may apply)
German citizens pursuing a Ph.D. abroad may also apply, but must provide an explanation for their choice of university; applications for a thesis abroad are assessed subject to available funds

At the time of application, the most recent degree must not be older than four years and three months (extensions only for pregnancy, childcare, extended illness or inability to work, and care of dependents; periods of professional qualification such as legal or teacher training do not count)

Applications may be submitted no earlier than the final semester of a master's programme or an equivalent course of study; funding can only begin once doctoral studies have started on a full-time basis

Part-time doctoral degrees cannot be funded; during the scholarship, Ph.D. candidates commit to concentrate fully on their dissertation, and parallel study on a taught degree or professional training programme is not compatible
Doctoral studies undertaken parallel to a medical degree are not eligible; funding is generally for the first doctoral degree only
requirements: Complete application pack submitted by mail (post only): printed on one side only and without staples, paper clips, folders or similar items, addressed to Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, Team Promotionsfoerderung, Ahrstr. 41, 53175 Bonn
Only complete applications received during a call will be considered in the selection process
Applications cannot be submitted twice; a rejection in the pre-selection or main selection is final, and the same applies to withdrawal from an ongoing procedure
A scientifically demanding and innovative doctoral project that can be completed within the three-year funding period, documented in a well-developed exposé
Evidence of individually organised studies and of broad extra-curricular interests and active commitment to social causes
Signed declaration on security-relevant aspects of the research project (required for non-EU applicants; the selection process cannot proceed without it)
documents: Completed application form (cover sheet for application) and questionnaire for applicants (both in German)
Questionnaire for the doctoral supervisor, completed by the first reviewer (an English version is available on the website)

Exposé of the proposed PhD project (German or English, maximum 20 pages) including working title, abstract, key terms, introduction, research question/problem, research status and own preparatory work, methods/provisional structure, schedule and work plan, and reference list
Curriculum vitae in both chronological and narrative formats

Reliable ranking/informative classification (typically an ECTS ranking or ECTS grade classification table) for the qualifying degree, plus degree certificate or provisional certificate with full transcript
Declaration on security-relevant aspects of the research project (non-EU applicants) and the proposal form for academic reviewers naming four or more eligible academics
selection_criteria: An ambitious and innovative Ph.D. proposal which can be completed within a three-year funding period
Effective supervision appropriate to the project and the doctoral candidate
Excellent degree results obtained within the regulation period of the study on the respective degree programme (guidance: among the top 15% of the year, judged across disciplinary cultures)
Evidence of broad extra-curricular interests and an active commitment and engagement with society at large

Two-stage review: pre-selection checks formal requirements and eligibility criteria (the exposé is not assessed at this stage); successful applications are reviewed by two qualified academics, with a second review including an interview with the candidate (usually via video call)
coverage: Monthly stipend of EUR 1,750 for doctoral study
Research allowance of up to EUR 100 paid at the end of each year to support academic work
Contribution of 50% of documented health insurance costs, up to EUR 170 a month, where insurance is not covered by employment
Family and childcare allowances, plus possible reallocation of funds from the final funding year ('time for money')
Grants for travel and additional living expenses for research trips, laboratory visits and conferences abroad
No institutional health or accident insurance cover, and no thesis printing cost allowance, is provided
application_method: Calls for applications are published approximately eight months before each selection meeting; each call remains open for two weeks (exactly 14 days) and there is no limit to the number of applications accepted.

Send the complete application documents via mail to Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, Team Promotionsfoerderung, Ahrstr. 41, 53175 Bonn, printed on one side only and without staples, paper clips or folders.
Applicants receive a short email informing them whether the application could be included in the selection process or whether the call had already closed.
After pre-selection (approx. six weeks) applicants are informed whether the application has been admitted to the main selection round; references are then requested from the named academic reviewers.

The second review includes an interview with the candidate, usually conducted via video call to minimise travel time and costs; the selection board for doctoral candidates then decides, normally within the respective call.
official.application_route: By post only - mail the complete application pack inside the open 14-day call window to the Bonn address; there is no online application.
official.study_mode: Full-time (part-time doctoral degrees cannot be funded; funding can only begin once doctoral studies have started on a full-time basis)
official.citizenship_residency: For doctorates at German universities, nationality is irrelevant. German citizens pursuing a Ph.D. abroad may apply with an explanation of the choice of university, subject to available funds; foreign nationals may submit the thesis abroad only if they obtained their higher education entrance qualification in Germany.
official.international_eligibility: Yes for doctoral study at a German university - the official FAQ states that non-German citizens completing a doctoral degree at a university in Germany can apply, and nationality is irrelevant on the application page.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No thematic, academic or regional focuses and no quotas (FAQ); any discipline is eligible, judged across different disciplinary cultures.
official.research_requirement: An exposé of the proposed PhD project (German or English, maximum 20 pages) with working title, abstract (approx. half a page), key terms, introduction, research question/problem/hypothesis, research status and own preparatory work, methods and provisional structure, schedule and work plan, and reference list; applications at an advanced stage of the dissertation are generally not considered.
official.duration: Initially three years, extendable by up to six months on application and subject to successful progress; on childbirth the maximum funding period is extended by 12 months for mothers and fathers, and mothers may take advantage of a three-month maternity protection period.
official.description: The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes supports 'the university education of young people who, because of their exceptional academic or artistic talents and personal qualities, can be expected to make an outstanding contribution to society as a whole', and its programmes include comprehensive financial and academic support for doctoral students. Applications are invited from highly qualified and socially committed PhD students, in conjunction with their academic supervisors.
official.program_type: Foundation-funded doctoral scholarship of the Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes for doctoral study and research in Germany
official.english_requirement: No IELTS/TOEFL or medium-of-instruction rule is published. The official FAQ states that application documents can be submitted in English and that an English version of the supervisor's questionnaire can be downloaded; the exposé of the proposed PhD project may be written in German or English (maximum 20 pages).

applicant_utility.summary: This is a strict-window, post-only scholarship: the current call runs 1-14 October 2026 and only complete paper applications received inside those 14 days enter the May 2027 selection, with the earliest possible start on 1 July 2027. Doctoral scholars receive a EUR 1,750 monthly stipend, up to EUR 100 a year research allowance, a health-insurance contribution of up to EUR 170 a month and travel grants for research and conferences - but no institutional insurance and no thesis printing allowance. Doctorates at German universities are open to applicants of any nationality, and the hard date filter is that your most recent degree is no older than four years and three months.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-performing doctoral candidates at German universities, of any nationality, whose last degree is under four years and three months old and who can document social engagement alongside an innovative project that can realistically finish within three years.
application_readiness_checklist: Diary the exact 14-day call window and post early - there is no online route and late arrivals are simply excluded
Download the current forms (application form and questionnaires are in German; an English version of the supervisor's questionnaire is available)
Ask your first reviewer to complete the supervisor questionnaire - the formal first reviewer assessing the thesis, not a postdoc day-to-day supervisor
Prepare an ECTS ranking or classification table for your qualifying degree plus a full transcript of all assessed coursework
Name four or more eligible academics as reviewers on the proposal form and do not contact them yourself
Sign the declaration on security-relevant aspects of the research project - the process cannot proceed without it
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete pack - only complete applications are considered, and documents are not returned to unsuccessful candidates
A most recent degree older than four years and three months without documented grounds (professional training such as the Referendariat does not extend the term)
Applying twice: a pre-selection or main-selection rejection is final, and withdrawing from an ongoing procedure counts as a rejection

A project that cannot plausibly be completed within the three-year funding period, or a late-stage application where the dissertation is largely written (advanced-stage applications are generally not considered)
Missing the supervisor's questionnaire, or failing the top-15% academic expectation for the relevant disciplinary culture
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Health insurance above the EUR 170 monthly contribution cap (there is no institutional insurance cover), travel to any in-person interview, thesis printing and publication costs, and any parallel taught degree or professional training, which the scholarship does not fund.
document_audit: Print single-sided, no staples, paper clips or folders, and use the postal address Team Promotionsfoerderung, Ahrstr. 41, 53175 Bonn
The exposé must be German or English and capped at 20 pages, with all required sections from working title to schedule and references
CV in both chronological and narrative formats; summary of the final thesis limited to two or three pages
If you apply before graduating, submit the transcript of records now and the degree certificate before the application goes to the board
alerts: The second-stage interview is usually a video call; if it is held in person you pay your own travel
Funding starts only once the doctorate is full-time - part-time doctorates cannot be funded and parallel teaching-degree or professional training is incompatible

Earliest start for the October 2026 call is 1 July 2027, so any existing funding must be able to end before that; you may not hold another doctoral scholarship at the same time and must report any other offers
The foundation gives no individual feedback on decisions, and former scholarship holders get no formal bonus even though alumni statistically fare better
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Post the complete pack inside the call window - confirmation email - pre-selection after about six weeks - two written academic reviews plus an interview (usually video) - selection board meeting for doctoral candidates - decision with a fixed scholarship start date.
